title: Liquid C2 and Graphiant Partner on Quantum-Secure Networking in Africa
html:
Insider Brief

  • Liquid C2 and Graphiant have partnered to offer African enterprises a managed Quantum Secure Network-as-a-Service (NaaS) combining post-quantum cryptography, secure connectivity and data sovereignty controls.
  • The service will connect branches, data centres, cloud environments and business partners through encrypted connectivity, network segmentation and centralised security policies.
  • The offering also includes network-level controls for AI and IoT traffic, allowing organisations to restrict destinations, monitor data routes and maintain auditable records of network activity.

PRESS RELEASE — Liquid C2, a business of Cassava Technologies, a global technology leader, and Graphiant (https://www.Graphiant.com/), a US-based provider of networking infrastructure built for AI, partnered to strengthen network security offerings through a new Quantum Secure Network-as-a-Service (NaaS). As quantum computing advances, it could eventually break the encryption that protects most data today. The proposition combines post-quantum cryptography (PQC), with encryption designed to withstand quantum attacks, with secure AI connectivity and data sovereignty security controls.

This helps African enterprises protect sensitive data against current and future threats, control where it goes, maintain a clear audit trail of its route, and simplify network management. Liquid C2 is bringing Graphiant’s security-first NaaS platform into a managed service that connects branches, data centres, cloud environments, and business partners. The offering combines encrypted connectivity, network segmentation, centralised security policies, and private cloud connections, giving customers greater visibility, analytic insights, and control without managing each connection as a separate project.

“Digital transformation is increasing the value of data to every organisation, but it is also expanding the risks around how that data is accessed, shared, and moved. To fully leverage cloud, AI, and connected operations, businesses must build cybersecurity and resilience into the foundations of their digital infrastructure. Incorporating Graphiant’s NaaS solution strengthens our ability to help customers create those foundations, while giving them the flexibility to grow, adapt, and innovate with confidence,” said Vinay Hiralall, Chief Commercial Officer, Liquid C2.

“When quantum computers break today’s encryption, it will happen for everyone at once, and Google has already set 2029 as its own migration deadline to become quantum-safe,” added Ali Shaikh, CEO at Graphiant. “Most organisations run thousands of applications, and updating each one in time isn’t realistic. Adding quantum protection to the network that connects them means one upgrade covers them all. This partnership brings that upgrade to African enterprises as a managed service, one that can migrate them to new algorithms as standards evolve.”

Cybersecurity challenges are constantly shifting, especially as AI moves from answering questions to taking action. AI agents connect to models, applications and partners, creating new routes through which sensitive information can move and be exposed. Through this solution, businesses will gain network-level visibility, access policies, and session tracing for AI connectivity, helping govern which destinations AI traffic can reach, retain evidence of those connections, and maintain greater control over their data.

As AI agents and connected (IoT) devices become increasingly autonomous, organisations need cybersecurity solutions that enforce security at the network layer, independent of the AI agent, application, or connected device itself. This solution prevents compromised AI agents or devices from accessing systems or moving laterally across networks or to destinations they were not meant to access. By offering sovereignty as an option and bringing these protections into a managed network service, operators can strengthen their digital foundations before risks become urgent.

Additionally, this solution allows customers to control which countries their network traffic passes through, encrypt it, and keep an auditable record of every route, ensuring compliance with regulators. This remote data sovereignty helps regulated organisations in finance, government, and healthcare move sensitive AI workloads onto Cassava AI Factories.

Data stolen today could be decrypted tomorrow. By combining post-quantum protection with managed connectivity, Liquid C2 and Graphiant are helping African enterprises secure their most valuable information well before quantum threats arrive, and adopt AI with control over where their data goes.
